clues: This place sits near the middle of its state, well inland from the sea. Leaders picked the spot so sea raids could not reach it fast.
Warm sea storms can crawl inland in late summer and dump days of heavy rain. In one month in 1999, rain here topped 21 inches.
This place was planned and built for one job: to be the seat of state government. Leaders picked the empty site in 1788, and the town was set up in 1792.
This place took its name from Sir Walter, a courtier of old England. He set up a colony on an island shore, and that colony was lost.
North Carolina state lawmakers meet in this place to pass laws. The governor of the state works here too.
